column2:
I would love to have one. Usually I just run around at the last minute scrambling to find the thing that will get delivered the quickest.
If I did have a philosophy, it would look something like:
1. Get souvenirs for people when travelling
2. If you're cooking something special for a lunchbox, carry extra, in a nice box if possible, especially if you know people like your cooking
3. For farewells and birthdays (if you're attending in person), always always include a handmade card / handwritten note with your gift
4. For birthdays / gifts / big-ticket gifts: the gift has to be some combination of the following, in order:
4.1 Something you've noticed this person really wants but would never buy for themselves because they think it's too much of an indulgence (expensive lip balm?? perfume?? desk organizer??)
4.2 Something novel, something this person loves but might not have come across (e.g. a thrift store that sells vintage cameras, knicknacks, a LEGO model of an F1 car they support, etc) -- the Internet is big, so your best bet is to put in the time and research
4.3 This isn't always possible but the best best gifts always have an element of surprise to them
4.4 Mock / joke gifts -- for close friends, try to include a joke gift, something cheap that references an inside joke or a habit

column2:
My philosophy is to not buy gifts for occasions rather while living your life whenever you come across something that reminds you of a person but it and then just wait for the right ocassion (if you have to ) . That's the occams razor version . 
Going into details - i
I generally devide my gifting into 3 categories -
1)Adhoc social acceptance gifts - these are obligatory gifts you give to people that you don't know enough to personalize. Here as much as I hate generic gifts things like silver coins , bouquet ( absolute waste of money personally) and the age old lifafa are the best . In general the gift is more determined by your relationship and the occasion/social norms . and unless your plan is to make an i.pression it's better to stick with safe bets .If you want to make a better impression buying gifts from neich luxury places are possible. Like expensive choclate or coffee beans things pople don't generally buy . Butyhis still requires some level of personal knowledge about the people you are gifting to . 
2) serendipitous-  here is where the philosophy i mentioned at the start really shines . Think of the gift as a medium what you really want to be sending is a message disguised as a present, for example I loved an artist friend of mine so for her birthday what I gave her was a website with all her art works ,( it was my way of showing my aprritiation for her artistic side ) or it could just be a reference of a event (one of friends stabbed me with a compass in school so I gave her a happy birthday card made entirely  otu of compasses those gifts were not given for utility. It was the sort of gift that has the right amount of schock factor and personal touch baked in . And The best way to get those is to just maintain a notes about whenever something reminded you of some one . 
3)The semi Known - this is the most difficult type of gifting these are times when you don't have anything serendipitous best sort of gift is the giving them something you know they need or premium supplies of hoobies /intrests theyight have . Having said that this can also allow you to occupy specific neiches is groups ( example - in my vast college group one the first couples that got married i gifted them a set of intimate toys as a joke 😅, but somehow that became the gift I gave to every friend on their wedding and apparently that's my role now )
